title: LLM Hallucinations as Ghost Theories via Formal-system Imitation
abstract: <div>  &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;Language-model hallucinations are usually judged one statement at a time. We argue that this pointwise view misses a structural mechanism. When an autoregressive model is trained on strings drawn from a formal system, it induces a stochastic inference graph; across bootstrap replicas this graph crystallises into an ensemble of weak formal systems. Some stable structures are genuine theorem-like regions anchored to the trusted axioms. Others are ghost theories: stable, internally coherent components generated by implicit ghost axioms but lacking a robust path back to the seed.&nbsp; </div> <div>  &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;The framework uses four ensemble observables: stability, axiom anchoring, logical damage, and bridge risk. Together they decompose the induced theory into an anchored core, true unanchored extensions, false floating ghost theories, and high-damage failures. We prove a soundness-based truth-uniformity result for connected components of the robust graph and explain ghost formation as a consequence of next-token training, which enforces local coherence without enforcing global genealogical closure. This also gives a topological account of paraconsistency: incompatible contents need not collapse the induced theory when they remain quarantined in disconnected components.&nbsp; </div> <div>  &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;Empirically, we study MIU and a bounded Robinson-Q-inspired arithmetic with equality and disequality. In MIU, anchoring reaches precision 0.976 against 0.640 for stability filtering at comparable recall. In the arithmetic setting, anchoring reaches precision 1.000 at the headline configuration, removing 33 stable false statements admitted by stability alone. The phenomenon transfers to a small Transformer trained from scratch; its largest false ghost cluster grows from 16 in the trigram setting to 38. Across 250 bootstraps spanning five independent seedbases every floating cluster is truth-uniform without exception, and approximately fifteen per cent of floating-cluster statements appear in floating clusters of every seedbase, identifying them as invariant biases of the model class on this formal system. Axiom-touch experiments further show that true-content touches yield new sound theorems, whereas false-content touches amplify falsity and sometimes break soundness without explicit contradiction. The resulting picture treats systematic hallucination not as isolated error, but as stable local inference structure without trusted genealogy. </div>

LLM-Based Operating Systems for Power System Relaying: A New Approach
abstract: Advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), present transformative opportunities for power system protection. This paper introduces an LLM-based operating system (LLM-OS) designed to enhance power system relaying. The proposed framework integrates LLMs to improve decision-making, fault detection, and adaptive protection schemes by leveraging natural language understanding and real-time data processing. Simulation studies validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the LLM-OS, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize relay operations and offering a roadmap for future implementations in the power industry.
